main_supplement_dependencies.text: The released VEMG2Pose estimator \cite{salter2024emg2pose} uses a fixed adapter retaining eight joint-flexion angles in radians. Source-domain validation (Table~S5), adapter, and scoring details are given in the Supplementary Methods. Cross-source calibration and temporal alignment remain unverified. Fig.~\ref{fig:substitution} separates the paired reference and estimated-input pathways.
Feature and training details are given in the Supplementary Methods.

The auxiliary fixed-threshold audit crosses two Score-only training configurations with two threshold objectives. Its disjoint development split and candidate threshold grid are detailed in the Supplementary Methods.

Historical N80 DB9 used paired-block budgets and a balanced endpoint on fixed common supported classes; the expansion uses prediction-valid budgets and requires every fixed reference class. Historical A20 tested frozen Boundary in two DB9 consumers. These protocols remain separate (Supplementary Tables~S1/S2).

Across N80 and A20, Full/U achieved positive median paired reductions relative to Boundary in all 24 consumer--budget comparisons within each cohort (Fig.~\ref{fig:ranking}). Direct comparisons with the learned Score-only/U control also favored Full/U in 23 of 24 N80 and 22 of 24 A20 comparisons (Supplementary Table~S3). At 30\% retention, the direct paired improvement reached 3.79 percentage points for CeTI grasp in N80.

Aggregate improvements did not describe how decision preservation was distributed across reference classes. At 30\% retention, Full/U achieved positive median paired overall reductions for all six consumers, while class-balanced changes varied in both direction and magnitude (Fig.~\ref{fig:fidelity}; Supplementary Table~S4).

Earlier frozen DB9 comparisons provide complementary evidence for selective retention and the role of decision geometry. Historical N80 Full selection at a 30\% paired-block budget reduced overall disagreement relative to Boundary by a median paired 3.47 percentage points (95\% participant-bootstrap interval: 1.87--4.76), and its fixed-common-class balanced endpoint improved by 9.14 percentage points (8.12--10.95) relative to the historical class-only learned selection baseline (\emph{class\_model}); both comparisons met their original prespecified sign-test criteria. Historical A20 Boundary comparisons and matched N80 feature-set contrasts remain separately reported in Supplementary Tables~S1 and S2.
